modules.name: Hub
modules.summary: hermes-hub and hermes-notify: push notifications, the System screen, file delivery, app updates.
modules.detail: A stdlib-only Python service on port 8791 that relays events to the phone, serves the System/Ops screens, uploads and media, and pairs the app. Also installs the hermes-notify command and the ops allowlist.

commands.name: curl
commands.why: used by the health check and several skills

files.why: the Hermes API server must be enabled with API_SERVER_KEY set

settings.prompt: Push relay URL (from the owner of the app; blank to skip)
GitHub repo for app updates, owner/name (blank to skip)
ntfy URL for local push (blank if unused)

modules.name: Companion skills
modules.summary: Ten Hermes skills for the phone, the homelab and daily life. Pick them one by one or take them all.
modules.detail: Skills follow the Hermes authoring standard (checked by check_skills.py). Installed into the Hermes skills folder under companion/. Edits you make to an installed skill are kept on update; the new version lands next to it as SKILL.md.kit-new.

modules.name: Phone actions for every channel
modules.summary: An MCP server that lets Hermes set alarms, send messages, call and more on your phone from any chat platform.
modules.detail: phone_mcp.py talks to the hub, which pushes each action to the Companion app. Registered in Hermes as the MCP server named 'phone'.

modules.name: Slash commands, undo and checkpoints
modules.summary: Hermes slash commands, edit/undo/regenerate and filesystem rollback from the app.
modules.detail: Runs 'hermes serve' on 127.0.0.1:9119 with a private token; only the hub talks to it. Needs the Python websockets package on the hub host.

commands.name: hermes
commands.why: hermes serve is part of the Hermes CLI

python_modules.name: websockets
python_modules.why: the hub reaches hermes serve over a WebSocket

modules.name: Codex remote
modules.summary: Continue Codex CLI sessions from the phone: watch, send, steer, stop and approve.
modules.detail: A bridge to the Codex app-server daemon plus the codex-rc command and the $rc Codex skill. Run codex-rc once to create its token and start the service.

commands.name: codex
commands.why: the Codex CLI (0.161 or newer) must be installed to have sessions to continue

python_modules.name: websockets
python_modules.why: the bridge talks to the Codex daemon over a WebSocket

modules.after: Run codex-rc once: it creates the bridge token, starts the service and notifies your phone.

modules.name: Claude Code bridge (experimental)
modules.summary: Claude Code from the phone through the Claude Agent SDK: its sessions, tool cards, approvals, steer, images and skills.
modules.detail: Installs the bridge into its own virtualenv and a service bound to 127.0.0.1:8792. Put an authenticated HTTPS or Tailscale proxy in front of it for phone access. Needs a Claude login for the user the service runs as.
modules.after: Edit CLAUDE_BRIDGE_CWD in the env file, then: systemctl enable --now hermes-claude-bridge

modules.name: Companion gateway platform
modules.summary: App chats run as gateway chats, like Telegram: risky commands and code ask for approval instead of being refused, Hermes can ask questions, cron results reach the phone.
modules.detail: Installs the companion platform plugin into Hermes. It serves the app's run API on port 8797 with the API server key and pushes messages sent outside a run through the hub. The app uses it for the main profile and falls back to the API server when it is out of reach.

files.why: the plugin authenticates the app with the API server key

modules.after: hermes plugins enable companion; hermes config set platforms.companion.enabled true; hermes config set display.platforms.companion.streaming true; hermes config set display.platforms.companion.tool_progress off; hermes config set plugins.stream_reasoning_deltas true; add COMPANION_HOME_CHANNEL=home to the Hermes .env; then systemctl restart hermes-gateway

modules.name: Proxmox status
modules.summary: Nodes, VMs and containers on the System screen, read over SSH (or pvesh when the hub runs on the Proxmox host).
modules.detail: Writes pve.json for the hub: the ssh target of the Proxmox host and a read-only key. Skip this if the hub runs on the Proxmox host itself.

modules.name: Speech-to-text server
modules.summary: Wyoming speech-to-text with live partial words (Parakeet TDT v3, GPU or CPU).
modules.detail: Port 10300 (10301 when the failover proxy runs on the same machine). Needs a Python virtualenv with onnx-asr; --stt-device gpu adds the NVIDIA CUDA 12 libraries. The model downloads on first start (about 600 MB).

modules.name: Text-to-speech server
modules.summary: Wyoming text-to-speech: natural English (Kokoro, 36 voices and mixes) and Bulgarian (Piper), optional Azure voices.
modules.detail: Port 10200. Downloads the Kokoro model (about 330 MB) and the Piper voices (about 120 MB) with --download-models. Azure neural voices switch on by putting AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION in voice.env (free tier capped at 450000 characters a month).

modules.name: Speech-to-text failover proxy
modules.summary: On the Hermes host: sends speech to your GPU box first and falls back to a local engine, so the app needs one address.
modules.detail: Listens on 10300. Set KIT_HOST and KIT_PORT in voice.env to the GPU box. Do not run it on the machine that also runs the main speech server unless that server uses port 10301.
